newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end higher with soybean futures.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end higher with soybean futures.

text.p: A supply-related rally in CBOT soybeans pushed soymeal and soyoil futures to end with moderate gains on Tuesday, floor traders said.
"The rally in beans is why everything closed higher," said one floor trader.
CBOT July soybeans settled 14-1/2 cents per bushel higher on concerns over scant U.S. supplies and fears that El Nino will produce drought in some counties this year, traders said.
Worry over soybean supplies were re-ignited after the widely watched Sparks Cos. of Memphis, Tenn. issued its 1996/97 (Aug/Sept) and 1997/98 ending stocks forecasts, traders said.

Sparks Companies put 1996/97 at 115 million bushels and 1997/98 at a small 123 million, floor sources said. The numbers were lower than the U.S. Department of Agriculture's old crop stocks estimate at 130 million bushels and new crop at 240 million bushels.
There were also rumors that West Coast livestock producers were importing soymeal from South America, traders said.
July soymeal settled up $2.30 at $278.70 per ton and other months were up $1.20 to $2.60. July soyoil closed up 0.11 at 23.24 cents and other months were up 0.08 to 0.20 cent a lb.
